keyFindings.description: rowBackedStates holds a block of N to its row by shownAskState (state, answered_by, answered_at; :61-66) and, for a decided row, by wording (:278-282). Two server-owned attributes settlement writes from the row are not held: selected and answer (askServerAttributeNames, ask_blocks.go:767; written at :792-800). A document-socket peer (any resolving caller, api/server.go:318-322; the file's own threat model at :28-29) overwrites a decided block's selected/answer, leaving the tuple and wording as the server wrote them; settlement's repair runs only at settlement; POST /artifacts/{id}/versions (authAny, routes_table.go:153) versions the live tree before it (NamedVersion -> captureLiveTextAndAuthors, no repair) and writeVersionTx runs the carry; with a human's answer to another block pending in the same window the verdict passes and an approved review in his name is pinned to a version whose block shows a selection and answer text he never gave, which the browser renders from those attributes (web/src/features/doc/ask-block.ts:171,192-193) and Show diff cannot expose (blocks cut). Second door at the same check: askNodes keeps the FIRST node of a repeated id (:249-253) and every check reads node.node, so a second ask node under a decided id with other wording passes - observed at the head with a throwaway docs test: a live-shaped tree holding two nodes under id `own` (the second asking 'Which region goes LAST?') gave rowBackedStates backed=true, the cut dropped both, and pmdoc.Render emitted the second body. Settlement renames repeats (stampBlockIDs) and restores attributes, so a settled version never has either; only the pre-settlement window does. Bounded as before: text outside blocks pinned, the row stays true, only a self-closed gate reopens; the record is wrong in the one place a reader takes for his decision. Fix in this pull request, one remedy for both: in rowBackedStates refuse a repeated id outright (askNodes already sees it; settlement calls it unreadable, ask_blocks.go:570-576), and hold the whole server-attribute set to the row with settlement's own writer - clone node.Attrs, run setAskServerAttributes(clone, ask, "", withhold) for withhold in {false, true}, accept only when one of the two reports changed == false (which keeps the legitimately withheld-answer block, ask_answers.go:50-63, carrying) - and replace the three-field shownAskState comparison with it. Unit cases in TestRowBackedStates... (forged selected; forged answer text; withheld answer accepted; repeated id refused) need no Postgres; an HTTP case through editLiveTree + POST /versions pins the door.

A block the approved version A did not hold, restored by the agent with the answer the human gave before A (the row stays answered across a deletion; settlement writes the answer back), is a block not as A held it and his, so the carry fires at settlement's version with no human action in the window. Content is his own question and answer; the companion case (A held it) now carries nothing and the CHANGELOG says so. Decide it: accept explicitly in the rule's comment and CHANGELOG, or require the changed block's row answer to be newer than the approval being carried (review.CreatedAt).

'Two candidates whose approvals both pass cannot happen by the rule's shape' (also packages/envoy/AGENTS.md) is not true: two candidates whose approved versions straddle a block's absence can both pass against different A's. Harmless at runtime (the guard at :199-201 carries nothing), but a future simplification trusting the sentence would drop the guard. Reword to 'should two pass, nothing is carried'.
